# noisylib

A one-function Python package built as a calibrated noise-floor fixture. `work(items)` folds the input into a 32-bit checksum and repeats that identical fold `WORK_UNITS` (1000) times, so its output depends only on the input while its running time is proportional to `WORK_UNITS`. Multiplying `WORK_UNITS` by `1 - p` is therefore a genuine speedup of exactly `p` on the timed work with byte-identical output, which is what `bench/run_bench.py --mode power` plants to measure the loop's acceptance rate against effect size. `run_tests.py` and `bench.py` are the frozen instruments: they print `METRIC name=value` lines for a research-loop harness; `bench.py` also prints `bench_work_ms` (sum of the timed repeats) so a caller can measure the instrument's fixed overhead as wall-clock minus timed work. No third-party dependencies; run `python3 run_tests.py` and `python3 bench.py` from this directory.
